title: Autonomic Latency Guardian and Recommender for Safe Batch/Cache Tuning
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Goal: Build an autonomic recommender that proposes batching and KV-cache configurations tailored to per-route traffic while enforcing latency/throughput SLO guardrails and providing safe apply/rollback paths. This ticket covers the recommender engine, an SLO-aware limiter layer, lightweight anomaly detection, and a controlled rollout harness for gradual application and automated rollback.

Background: Many customers see token-cost savings after applying more aggressive batching/prefetch settings but suffer intermittent latency spikes due to traffic skew, tail events, or model sequence-length changes. Existing advisories are manual and siloed. We need an automated pipeline that outputs candidate configs, simulates expected performance, enforces SLO constraints, and applies changes via staged cohorts with circuit-breakers.

Scope:
- Recommender: ingest per-route telemetry (latency histograms, seq-length distribution, qps), propose batch_size, prefetch_kv, batching_window ms, and quantization hints.
- SLO Guard: enforce hard SLO thresholds (p99 latency, error rate) as preconditions and runtime limiters that throttle recommendations into safe buckets.
- Anomaly Detector: lightweight streaming detector for sudden shifts in tail latency, request size, or error rate; flags and blocks applies.
- Safe Apply Harness: staged cohorts (shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automatic rollback triggers based on SLO breach or metric drift.
- Observability: dashboard prototype and alert rules for canary windows, plus audit logs for any automated apply/rollback event.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces candidate configs for at least three sample routes with expected cost delta and simulated latency delta.
SLO Guard rejects any candidate where simulated p99 exceeds target or where error-rate regression > 0.5% absolute.
Safe Apply Harness can stage a config through shadow -> 1% -> 10% with automated rollback if p99 increases by more than 20% or error rate doubles.
Anomaly Detector flags sudden distribution shifts within 5 minutes and blocks automated applies until cleared.
Dashboard displays per-cohort metrics, apply/rollback history, and per-route recommended savings estimates.
Unit and integration tests covering recommender logic, guard checks, and rollback triggers included in PRs.
notes: 2025-02-15: Kickoff sync with PM and Observability. Agreed to reuse existing telemetry pipeline (metrics-v2) and add a small dedupe layer for route bucketing.
2025-02-20: Design decision - simulate latency using a micro-simulator that samples seq-length and qps instead of running canary for every candidate to control cost.
2025-02-25: Trade-off: stronger batching yields cost savings but increases tail variance. Chosen approach is conservative recommendations with multi-window simulation (1m, 10m, 1h).
2025-02-28: Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3892 - initial recommender + unit tests. Needs integration tests and observability links.
2025-03-02: UX sync with Console team - acceptance criteria for dashboard metrics solidified. Link to spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Latency+Guardian+Recommender+Spec
2025-03-03: Implemented stub for anomaly detector. Next: wire into apply harness and add audit logging to events table.
steps_to_validate: 1) Run simulation job for route 'chat/default' for last 24h traffic and review candidate list + simulated p99 and cost delta.
2) Apply candidate to a shadow cohort and verify no change in production latency and no errors reported for 30 minutes.
3) Progress to 1% cohort; monitor p50/p95/p99 and error-rate for 60 minutes; verify no SLO breach.
4) If any automatic rollback triggers, inspect audit logs and anomaly detector flags; file follow-up ticket if rollback due to false-positive.
5) Run canary with synthetic tail queries to validate recommender safety for long-sequence requests.
